what_this_is: The row sources a list may declare (row_sources: [{ source, id?, root?, of, match?, exclude?, paths?, text_extensions?, content?, values? }]) and the tool that serves each. source is the tool kind; optional id is its unique logical collection identity, defaulting to source for existing lists. Each template input uses the declared source fields, retaining exact JSON types; absent optional inputs are omitted. content, exclude, paths and text_extensions are forwarded unchanged. values projects fields while retaining every original value. limit and after bound each page. A refresh streams all successful pages before it removes obsolete rows, regardless of a view's rows_per_read bound. A new source kind is one row here. A source declared original: "list" (with optional adopt_own_rows and copy_name) is the list's copy instead of its origin: its refresh is the two-way sync of list-copy.mjs, through the source kind's change tool, and only a source kind with change and copy can be one.

restore.why: The account's restore generation (list-copy.mjs invariant 6): the setting record stamped when the account adopts an older copy of its state, { value: { generation, restored_at } }. A two-way sync trusts no removal judged from a row version older than restored_at, so a restore never deletes the newer file copies: they are carried back up. With no such record the account was never restored and every removal is judged as before.

copies_when_unreachable.why: When a list's file copy may be read, read-only (copy-readable.mjs, asked by a copy guard): only when reading the list answers one of these codes, or the door cannot be reached at all (transport_failures), which is when every holder of the account is unreachable. Any answer from the list, with or without rows, keeps the copy closed, so agents read the list. On Nov 3, 2026 the account's stores were lost and the door answered original_workspace_source_unavailable for hours while the copies held every memory.

measured.on: 2026-11-13 CST, Mac load average 12 to 18, other lanes writing

writes.source: one library row and four library rows (22 KB) alternately every 2 s for 15 min; the door bounds one call at 5 s (trillion-rust legacy_records Bounds elapsed), so a write over 5 s the door may still answer but the next may be refused write_deadline_exceeded

busy_episodes.source: the busy log lines of the committed refresh at 18:58 CST, records:list calls that landed after 5 retries

measured.budget: waits of 200 ms doubling for 7 retries sum to 25.4 s, the first budget past the longest episode seen (20.8 s). Two episodes are a small sample: read ~/Library/Logs/list-reader-door-busy.jsonl as it grows and move retries to cover its longest waited_ms.

door_retry.why: A call the door refused as busy and never started (HTTP 503, selected_owner_unavailable, write_deadline_exceeded, original_workspace_source_unavailable) or whose outcome is unknown is sent again with the same request key after first_wait_ms, doubling, up to retries times. measured is what the busy_log lines and a write sampler showed under real load; the budget is set from it, not picked.

limits.why: planned_shown: the most planned actions a dry run of a two-way sync lists; its counts are always whole.The bounds of a list read and a refresh, kept by the list reader because reading a list is this tool's job (the engine stores and lists records; it reads no list). read_page_rows: rows a page holds when the caller names no limit, and the most one source tool's page asks for. door_page_rows: the most one records:list asks for, the records door's own page (records-door.json list_page; the door cuts any page to one message). rows_per_read: the most rows one view read gathers, including rules or a sort; a refresh streams as many bounded pages as a source needs and is not capped at that view bound. row_sources_per_list: the most row sources one list may declare (8 since 2026-11-05: the Library declares six, its sixth the knowledge folder's hidden files by exact path, which a folder scan skips). write_rows and write_bytes: the most records and bytes one records:write of a refresh sends (the door answers within one 65,536-byte message, and the step-4 sends of export-records-as-list-rows use the same 64 and 24,000).

documents.about: the markdown documents in a folder the person granted; each document a row, its frontmatter its fields (tools/documents-as-list-rows). As a list's copy (original: list), tool:change-a-document-row writes a whole document or removes one only while it is still the one read; copy names the fields that hold a document's text, its parts and the identity of the file a row was made from

json-items.about: the items of one JSON file at one path (rules, checks, any objects with an id; tools/documents-as-list-rows read-data/json-items.mjs): each item a row holding its keys as they are, its JSON text copy.text; a list names its own fields (a switch, who judges the row) in its source content.list_only, and those never reach the file. As a list's copy (original: list), tool:change-a-json-item-row writes or removes one item only while it is still the one read and keeps the rest of the file

namespace-documents.about: the markdown documents in a folder of the person's Namespace files, read through the files door; each document a row, its frontmatter its fields (tools/documents-as-list-rows)
